sections.text: From Stuxnet to FrostyGoop, attacks now target the controllers themselves.
So... are your controllers compromised? Right now?
Configs are rarely checked against a golden baseline.
Vendor tools work one device at a time, need a Windows VM per vendor, and can cost eleven thousand dollars a seat.
What if one tool could see them all?
Meet PEAT. The Process Extraction and Analysis Tool, from Sandia National Laboratories.
Scan finds and fingerprints O-T devices.
Pull grabs logic, configs, logs, and firmware, over Ethernet or serial.
Parse turns proprietary blobs into one data model.
Then diff it against your golden config, or stream it into Elastic or Splunk.
Ten-plus vendors. Linux, Windows, or Docker.
And it's completely free. Open source, under GPL version three.
Close the visibility gap. Get PEAT on GitHub today.
